newsitem.title: USA: S. Africa finmin looks at liberalization criteria.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa finmin looks at liberalization criteria.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said Saturday he favored liberalization of the rand, and that a comfortable level of reserves would be a key factor in the decision to remove exchange controls.

Manuel, speaking before the Institute for International Finance, said he could not indicate a specific date for lifting controls. Instead, the timing for liberalization would depend on a set of economic variables, among which would be a 12 week reserve-to-import cover, he added.
"It's not the kind of decision that you can set a timetable for," Manuel said. "We would have to evaluate circumstances."

"The level of reserves would certainly be right at the top of determinants rather than any arbitrary timetable," he added. "Certainly we would want a sufficient comfort level of 12 weeks (reserves/import cover)."
South Africa currently has about a reserve cover of about one month, down from nine weeks in January, Manuel said.

Manuel said his liberalization goal did not contradict the postion of the International Monetary Fund, which said Saturday the country should continue to improve its standing in financial markets before eliminating exchange controls.
"There is no contradiction," Manuel said. "I dont think there is any conflict between that which we have said and that which the Fund advises."
An IMF official said the Fund has supported the gradual elimination of exchange controls for South Africa because liberalization should proceed when the risk of disruption is minimized.

The South African rand has undergone intense volatility and been subject to market speculators this year, setting record lows as it depreciated against the U.S. dollar. The rand ended trade Friday at 4.53 per dollar, down from 3.65 in February.

The minister said he would be starting a roadshow through the United States next week to promote the country's planned Yankee bond issue, but he said he could not yet determine the size or price of the issue.
"Those decisions will be taken once we test the market," Manuel said. "We will make a decision based on the response scheduled by the maturity profile and the price."
